extracted.intended_audience: aspiring stand-up comedians, comedy writers, and owners/readers of Judy Carter’s The New Comedy Bible
extracted.subtask_description: A workbook-based method for creating, capturing, workshopping, and polishing stand-up jokes and structuring sets. Emphasizes daily writing prompts, topical organization, iterative drafting, and portable digital capture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create, capture, and hone pro comedy material
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a proven method for creating, capturing, and honing pro comedy material; think of it as a 'how-to' manual for building a comedy career, joke by joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on a pipeline: generate ideas, record/capture them immediately, and iteratively refine until performance-ready. The workbook is presented as the tool to manage that process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turn problems into punchlines (48 exercises)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1: 48 Exercises to Turn Problems into Punchlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured exercises to mine personal problems or situations and reframe them into comedic premises and punchlines. The specific number (48) implies repeated practice and varied prompts to build material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshopping jokes in progress by topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2: Jokes in Progress by Topic (Place to write & workshop material in progress).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize draft jokes by topic so you can workshop and revise them over time; treat this section as a staging area for ideas not yet polished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polish final jokes by topic (My Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3: My Act: Polished Jokes by Topic (Final resting place of your comedy gems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move finished, performance-ready jokes into a polished collection organized by topic. This serves as the canonical set of material to perform and refine for audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan set lists by time and theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4: Set Lists (Place to store the running order of your act based on time & theme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange jokes into running order tailored to set length and thematic flow. Use set lists to manage pacing, callbacks, and transitions appropriate to allotted time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use morning writings/writing prompts to generate material
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5: Morning Writings (30 writing prompts to create material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a regular writing habit (e.g., morning prompts) to force idea generation and keep material fresh. The workbook supplies 30 prompts to jumpstart daily practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture work in a portable, editable digital format
rubrics_metrics.description: This special PDF version works on all devices including PCs, Macs, Chrome, Apple and Android phones and other devices. You can type in your work, save it and have it available across all devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a fillable, cross-device format so you can capture ideas on the go, keep them synchronized, and edit drafts digitally rather than relying solely on loose notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop an authentic comedic persona
rubrics_metrics.description: Helps others find their authentic persona and communicate it in a way that makes audiences laugh. (Endorsement quote from Lily Tomlin.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize discovering and expressing a genuine stage persona as central to making material land; exercises are designed to surface authentic voice and viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use incremental, joke-by-joke career-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Described as a method for building a comedy career, joke by joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat career development as cumulative: continuously generate, refine, and perform jokes so that small improvements and a growing inventory of polished material build a professional path.
